summary.text: Nucleic acids are large biomolecules, crucial in all cells and viruses, composed of nucleotides.
The two main classes are DNA and RNA, which differ in whether the sugar is deoxyribose or ribose.
They carry information in cells, make up genetic material, and both play a crucial role in directing protein synthesis.

facts.label: Building block
facts.value: A nucleotide: a sugar, a phosphate and a base

facts.label: Thymine and uracil
facts.value: Thymine only in DNA, uracil only in RNA

facts.label: Biggest molecule
facts.value: Human chromosome 1: 247 million base pairs in one molecule

facts.label: Name
facts.value: Richard Altmann created the term in 1889

facts.label: 1944 experiment
facts.value: Showed that DNA carries genetic information

items.prompt: A chain of nucleotides has deoxyribose as its sugar and contains thymine. Which nucleic acid is it?

options.label: RNA
DNA
Neither, since nucleic acids use no sugar
A nucleoside

items.explain: If the sugar is deoxyribose the polymer is DNA, and thymine occurs in DNA.

items.prompt: A researcher checks a bacterial cell and a typical virus for DNA and RNA. What should she expect?

options.label: The cell holds both, while the virus usually holds just one
Both hold both kinds in equal amounts
The cell holds only DNA, and the virus holds only RNA
Neither holds RNA, since RNA is found only in the nucleus

items.explain: All living cells contain both DNA and RNA, while viruses contain either DNA or RNA, but usually not both.

items.prompt: Why do the two ends of a nucleic acid strand differ from each other?

options.label: One end of the strand carries a base while the other end carries none at all
One end of the strand is made of DNA while the other end is made of RNA
Phosphates attach at the 3' and 5' carbons of the sugar, giving the strand a direction
The sugars and the bases alternate in turn all the way along the chain

items.explain: The phosphate groups attach to the 3'-end and 5'-end carbons of the sugar, which gives nucleic acids directionality.

items.prompt: A scientist finds a virus whose genome is double-stranded RNA. Is that impossible?

options.label: Yes, RNA is always single-stranded
Yes, only DNA can form a genome in a virus
No, but only because the virus has stolen DNA from a cell
No, some viruses do have double-stranded RNA genomes

items.explain: Most natural DNA is double-stranded and RNA single-stranded, but some viruses have double-stranded RNA genomes.

items.prompt: What two things led to the name 'nucleic acid'?

options.label: They were first found in the nucleus, and they contain phosphate groups
They were first found in pus, and they contain amino acids
They are found only in the nucleus, and they dissolve in acid
They are found in viruses, and they contain no sugar

items.explain: Nucleic acids were named for their discovery within the nucleus and for the presence of phosphate groups.

items.prompt: Which part of a nucleotide makes the whole molecule acidic?

options.label: The nitrogenous base
The phosphate group
The pentose sugar
The sugar's missing hydroxyl group

items.explain: Each nucleotide has a nucleobase, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group which makes the molecule acidic.
